title: Bekhorot 60
description: How the count under the rod goes wrong: Rav Huna bar Seḥora’s two-opening pen, two animals that emerge as one, the mishna on a miscalled ninth, tenth and eleventh, and Rava’s cases of two animals that come out together.
topics: 🐑 Nineteen lambs: Rav Huna bar Seḥora’s pen with two openings
🔢 Counting pair by pair or by the hundred: Rav Mari and Rav Kahana on Rabbi Yoḥanan
🔁 Counting backward, and the Persians who call ten “one”
⚠️ The ninth, tenth and eleventh miscalled: Rabbi Meir and Rabbi Yehuda
📏 Only the neighbors of the tenth are sanctified by mistake, and Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Shimon’s single mistake
👯 Rava: two animals that emerge together at the ninth or the tenth
🗣️ Has the name “tenth” been removed? Rav Kahana, Rav Ashi and Rabbi’s “aḥad asar”
⚖️ The tenth and eleventh intermingled: graze, be sacrificed, or die

a1.he: לֹא יֹאמַר: אֶבְרוֹר עֲשָׂרָה וְאֶטּוֹל מֵהֶן אֶחָד וְהַשְּׁאָר פְּטוּרִים, אֶלָּא כּוֹנְסָן לַדִּיר, וּמוֹצִיא עֲשָׂרָה, וְנוֹטֵל מֵהֶן אֶחָד, וְהַשְּׁאָר מִצְטָרְפִין לְגוֹרֶן אַחֵר.

a2.he: וְהָתַנְיָא: תִּשְׁעָה עָשָׂר טְלָאִים, לֹא יֹאמַר: אֶבְרוֹר עֲשָׂרָה וְאֶטּוֹל מֵהֶן אֶחָד, וְהַשְּׁאָר פְּטוּרִין, אֶלָּא כּוֹנְסָן לַדִּיר, וּמוֹצִיא עֲשָׂרָה וְנוֹטֵל מֵהֶן אֶחָד, וְהַשְּׁאָר פְּטוּרִין.

a3.he: תַּרְגְּמַהּ רַב הוּנָא בַּר סְחוֹרָה קַמֵּיהּ דְּרָבָא בְּרִיגְלָא: בְּדִיר שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ שְׁנֵי פְתָחִים עָסְקִינַן, וְיָצְאוּ תִּשְׁעָה בְּפֶתַח זֶה וְתִשְׁעָה בְּפֶתַח זֶה, דְּהַאיְךְ חַד חָזֵי לְהָכָא וּלְהָכָא.

a4.he: וְלִישַׁנֵּי לֵיהּ: כְּגוֹן שֶׁמָּנָה תִּשְׁעָה, וְכִי מְטָא עֲשָׂרָה קָרֵי ״חַד״ מֵרֵישָׁא! קָסָבַר: עֲשִׂירִי מֵאֵלָיו קָדוֹשׁ.

a5.he: וְלִישַׁנֵּי לֵיהּ בְּגוֹרֶן, וּמְנָאָן זוּגוֹת זוּגוֹת! קָסָבַר: עֲשִׂירִי לְמִנְיָן בְּהֵמוֹת הוּא קָדוֹשׁ.

a6.he: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק: זְכַאי אִימֵּיהּ דְּרַב הוּנָא בַּר סְחוֹרָה, דְּשַׁנִּי לֵיהּ שְׁמַעְתָּא בְּרִיגְלָא כִּשְׁמַעְתֵּיהּ.

a7.he: מַתְנִי׳ יָצְאוּ שְׁנַיִם כְּאַחַת — מוֹנֶה אוֹתָם שְׁנַיִם שְׁנַיִם, מְנָאָן אֶחָד — תְּשִׁיעִי וַעֲשִׂירִי מְקוּלְקָלִין.

a8.he: קָרָא לַתְּשִׁיעִי ״עֲשִׂירִי״, וְלָעֲשִׂירִי ״תְּשִׁיעִי״, וְלָאַחַד עָשָׂר ״עֲשִׂירִי״ — שְׁלָשְׁתָּן מְקוּדָּשִׁין: הַתְּשִׁיעִי נֶאֱכָל בְּמוּמוֹ, וְהָעֲשִׂירִי מַעֲשֵׂר, וְאַחַד עָשָׂר קָרֵב שְׁלָמִים וְעוֹשֶׂה תְּמוּרָה, דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי מֵאִיר.

a9.he: אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה: וְכִי יֵשׁ תְּמוּרָה עוֹשָׂה תְּמוּרָה? אָמְרוּ מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי מֵאִיר: אִילּוּ הָיָה תְּמוּרָה — לֹא הָיָה קָרֵב. קָרָא לַתְּשִׁיעִי ״עֲשִׂירִי״, וְלָעֲשִׂירִי ״עֲשִׂירִי״, וְלָאַחַד עָשָׂר ״עֲשִׂירִי״ — אֵין אַחַד עָשָׂר מְקוּדָּשׁ. זֶה הַכְּלָל: כֹּל שֶׁלֹּא נֶעֱקַר שֵׁם עֲשִׂירִי מִמֶּנּוּ, אֵין אַחַד עָשָׂר מְקוּדָּשׁ.

a10.he: גְּמָ׳ אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: מְנָאָן זוּגוֹת זוּגוֹת, קִינְטָרִין קִינְטָרִין — עֲשִׂירִי לְמִנְיָנוֹ הוּא קָדוֹשׁ.

a11.he: ״לְמִנְיָנוֹ״ מַאי? רַב מָארִי אָמַר: לַמִּנְיָן שֶׁלּוֹ הוּא קָדוֹשׁ, רַב כָּהֲנָא אָמַר: לְמִנְיַן בְּהֵמוֹת הוּא קָדוֹשׁ.

a12.he: תְּנַן: יָצְאוּ שְׁנַיִם כְּאַחַת — מוֹנֶה אוֹתָן שְׁנַיִם שְׁנַיִם. מְנָאָן אֶחָד — תְּשִׁיעִי וַעֲשִׂירִי מְקוּלְקָלִין.

a13.he: בִּשְׁלָמָא לְמַאן דְּאָמַר: לַמִּנְיָן שֶׁלּוֹ הוּא קָדוֹשׁ, מִשּׁוּם הָכִי הָווּ תְּשִׁיעִי וַעֲשִׂירִי מְקוּלְקָלִין, וְלָעֲשִׂירִי קָא קָרֵי לֵיהּ ״תְּשִׁיעִי״, וְלָאַחַד עָשָׂר ״עֲשִׂירִי״. אֶלָּא לְמַאן דְּאָמַר: לְמִנְיַן בְּהֵמוֹת הוּא קָדוֹשׁ, לַתְּשִׁיעִי ״תְּשִׁיעִי״ קָא קָרֵי לֵיהּ, וְלָעֲשִׂירִי ״עֲשִׂירִי״ קָא קָרֵי לֵיהּ!

a14.he: אָמַר לָךְ רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: כִּי אָמֵינָא אֲנָא — הֵיכִי דְּאִיכַּוֵּין לְאַפּוֹקֵי זוּגוֹת זוּגוֹת, הֵיכָא דִּנְפַק מִמֵּילָא — לָא.

a15.he: תָּא שְׁמַע: מְנָאָן לְמַפְרֵעַ — עֲשִׂירִי שֶׁבְּמִנְיָן הוּא קָדוֹשׁ. בִּשְׁלָמָא לְמַאן דְּאָמַר לְמִנְיַן בְּהֵמוֹת הוּא קָדוֹשׁ — שַׁפִּיר, אֶלָּא לְמַאן דְּאָמַר לַמִּנְיָן שֶׁלּוֹ הוּא קָדוֹשׁ, עֲשִׂירִי ״חַד״ קָרֵי לֵיהּ!

a16.he: אָמַר רָבָא: הוֹאִיל וְאִיתֵיהּ בְּמִנְיָנָא פָּרְסָאָה, דְּקָרוּ לְעַשְׂרָה ״חַד״.

b1.he: קָרָא לַתְּשִׁיעִי ״עֲשִׂירִי״, וְלָעֲשִׂירִי ״תְּשִׁיעִי״, וְלָאַחַד עָשָׂר ״עֲשִׂירִי״. תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: מִנַּיִן שֶׁאִם קָרָא לַתְּשִׁיעִי ״עֲשִׂירִי״, וְלָעֲשִׂירִי ״תְּשִׁיעִי״, וְלָאַחַד עָשָׂר ״עֲשִׂירִי״, שֶׁשְּׁלָשְׁתָּן מְקוּדָּשִׁין?

b2.he: תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: ״וְכׇל מַעְשַׂר בָּקָר וָצֹאן כֹּל אֲשֶׁר יַעֲבוֹר תַּחַת הַשָּׁבֶט הָעֲשִׂירִי יִהְיֶה קֹּדֶשׁ״, יָכוֹל שֶׁאֲנִי מְרַבֶּה אַף שְׁמִינִי וּשְׁנֵים עָשָׂר?

b3.he: אָמְרַתְּ: הוֹאִיל וְהוּא קָדוֹשׁ, וְטָעוּתוֹ מִתְקַדֶּשֶׁת, מָה הוּא אֵינוֹ מְקוּדָּשׁ אֶלָּא בְּסָמוּךְ, אַף טָעוּתוֹ אֵינָהּ מִתְקַדֶּשֶׁת אֶלָּא בְּסָמוּךְ.

b4.he: וְהָתַנְיָא: מָה הוּא מְיוּחָד, אַף טָעוּתוֹ מְיוּחֶדֶת!

b5.he: תָּאנֵי תַּנָּא קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: הָא מַנִּי? רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן הִיא, דְּתַנְיָא: רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר: לְעוֹלָם אֵין אַחַד עָשָׂר קָדוֹשׁ עַד שֶׁיִּשְׁתּוֹק בַּתְּשִׁיעִי, וְיִקְרָא לָעֲשִׂירִי ״תְּשִׁיעִי״, וְלָאַחַד עָשָׂר ״עֲשִׂירִי״.

b6.he: סָבַר לַהּ כְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה, דְּאָמַר: טָעוּת מַעֲשֵׂר תְּמוּרָה הָוֵי, וְסָבַר לַהּ כַּאֲבוּהּ, דְּאָמַר: אֵין מֵימֵר חוֹזֵר וּמֵימֵר.

b7.he: אָמַר רָבָא: יָצְאוּ שְׁנַיִם בַּתְּשִׁיעִי, קְרָאָן ״תְּשִׁיעִי״ — עֲשִׂירִי וְחוּלִּין מְעוֹרָבִין זֶה בָּזֶה, עֲשִׂירִי מֵאֵלָיו קָדוֹשׁ, לַתְּשִׁיעִי ״תְּשִׁיעִי״ קָא קָרֵי לֵיהּ.

b8.he: קְרָאָן ״עֲשִׂירִי״, עֲשִׂירִי וּתְשִׁיעִי מְעוֹרָבִין זֶה בָּזֶה. מַאי טַעְמָא? ״עֲשִׂירִי״ קָא קָרֵי לְהוּ לְתַרְוַיְיהוּ.

b9.he: יָצְאוּ שְׁנַיִם בָּעֲשִׂירִי וּקְרָאָן ״עֲשִׂירִי״, עֲשִׂירִי וְאַחַד עָשָׂר מְעוֹרָבִין זֶה בָּזֶה. קְרָאָן ״אַחַד עָשָׂר״, עֲשִׂירִי וְחוּלִּין מְעוֹרָבִין זֶה בָּזֶה.

b10.he: הָא תּוּ לְמָה לִי? הַיְינוּ הָךְ! הָא קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן: דְּכֹל בַּת אַחַת תַּרְוַויְיהוּ קָא קָדְשִׁי, וְאַף עַל גַּב דְּלֹא נֶעֱקַר שֵׁם ״עֲשִׂירִי״ הֵימֶנּוּ.

b11.he: יָתֵיב רַב כָּהֲנָא וְקָאָמַר לֵיהּ לְהָא שְׁמַעְתָּא, אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אָשֵׁי לְרַב כָּהֲנָא: וַהֲלֹא לֹא נֶעֱקַר שֵׁם ״עֲשִׂירִי״ הֵימֶנּוּ, וּתְנַן זֶה הַכְּלָל: כׇּל זְמַן שֶׁלֹּא נֶעֱקַר שֵׁם ״עֲשִׂירִי״ הֵימֶנּוּ — אֵין אַחַד עָשָׂר מְקוּדָּשׁ! הָנֵי מִילֵּי בְּזֶה אַחַר זֶה, אֲבָל בְּבַת אַחַת — תַּרְוַיְיהוּ קָא קָדְשִׁי.

b12.he: זֶה אַחַר זֶה — בְּהֶדְיָא קָתָנֵי לַהּ: קָרָא לַתְּשִׁיעִי ״עֲשִׂירִי״, וְלָעֲשִׂירִי ״עֲשִׂירִי״, וְלָאַחַד עָשָׂר ״עֲשִׂירִי״ — אֵין אַחַד עָשָׂר מְקוּדָּשׁ. ״זֶה הַכְּלָל״ לְאֵיתוֹיֵי מַאי? לָאו לְאֵיתוֹיֵי בְּבַת אַחַת?

b13.he: לָא, לְאֵיתוֹיֵי יָצָא עֲשִׂירִי וְלֹא דִּבֵּר, דְּהָא לֹא נֶעֱקַר שֵׁם ״עֲשִׂירִי״ הֵימֶנּוּ.

b14.he: דְּאִי לָא תֵּימָא הָכִי, הָא דְּתַנְיָא: יָצְאוּ שְׁנַיִם בָּעֲשִׂירִי, וְלֹא קָדַם אֶחָד מֵהֶן אֶת חֲבֵירוֹ, וּקְרָאָן ״עֲשִׂירִי״ — עֲשִׂירִי וְאַחַד עָשָׂר מְעוֹרָבִין זֶה בָּזֶה, וַהֲלֹא לֹא נֶעֱקַר שֵׁם עֲשִׂירִי הֵימֶנּוּ! אֶלָּא לָאו מִשּׁוּם דְּאָמְרִינַן: כֹּל בְּבַת אַחַת תַּרְוַיְיהוּ קָא קָדְשִׁי.

b15.he: אִי מִשּׁוּם הָא לָא אִירְיָא, הָכָא בְּמַאי עָסְקִינַן? דִּקְדֵים חַד מִינַּיְיהוּ וְאַפֵּיק לְרֵישֵׁיהּ, וְקַרְיֵיהּ ״אַחַד עָשָׂר״, וַהֲדַר אִיעָרוּב וּנְפוּק בַּהֲדָדֵי, וּקְרִינְהוּ ״עֲשִׂירִי״, דְּהָא נֶעֱקַר שֵׁם עֲשִׂירִי הֵימֶנּוּ.

b16.he: וְהָא ״לֹא קָדַם״ קָתָנֵי! מַאי ״לֹא קָדַם״? דַּהֲדַר אִיעָרוּב.

b17.he: וּכְמַאן? דְּלָא כְּרַבִּי, דְּאִי רַבִּי — הָאָמַר: ״אַחַד עָשָׂר״ לָא הָוֵי עֲקִירָה!

b18.he: אֲפִילּוּ תֵּימָא רַבִּי, כִּי אָמַר רַבִּי הֵיכָא דְּאִית לֵיהּ בְּהֵמוֹת טוּבָא, דְּאָמְרִינַן: חַד עִישּׂוּרָא קָאָמַר, הָכָא דְּלֵית לֵיהּ בְּהֵמוֹת טְפֵי.

b19.he: מַאי רַבִּי? דְּתַנְיָא: קָרָא לַעֲשִׂירִי ״אַחַד עָשָׂר״, וְלָאַחַד עָשָׂר ״עֲשִׂירִי״ — אֵין אַחַד עָשָׂר קָדוֹשׁ, דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי. רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: אַחַד עָשָׂר קָדוֹשׁ. כְּלָל אָמַר רַבִּי: כׇּל זְמַן שֶׁלֹּא נֶעֱקַר שֵׁם עֲשִׂירִי הֵימֶנּוּ — אֵין אַחַד עָשָׂר קָדוֹשׁ. אָמַר רָבָא: הָכָא בְּמַאי עָסְקִינַן? כְּגוֹן דְּאִית לֵיהּ בְּהֵמוֹת טוּבָא, דְּאָמְרִינַן: חַד עִישּׂוּרָא קָאָמַר.

b20.he: יָצְאוּ שְׁנַיִם בָּעֲשִׂירִי, תָּנֵי חֲדָא: יִרְעוּ, וְתַנְיָא אִידַּךְ: יִקְרְיבוּ, וְתַנְיָא אִידַּךְ: יָמוּתוּ.

b21.he: לָא קַשְׁיָא, הָא דְּתַנְיָא יִרְעוּ — רַבָּנַן הִיא, דְּאָמְרִי: אֵין מְבִיאִין קָדָשִׁים לְבֵית הַפְּסוּל״

messages.text: Continued from 59b: Rava ruled that one who has fifteen lambs may not pick out ten and exempt the rest, and the Gemara cites a baraita that teaches the same: “If one had fifteen lambs, …”

… he may not say: I will separate ten and bring them into the pen, and I will take one of them as animal tithe, and the rest will be exempt. Rather, he must bring them all into the pen and remove ten of them by causing them to emerge from the opening, and take one of them, the tenth one, as animal tithe. And the remainder combine with animals born later, to be tithed in another designated time of gathering.

notes.he: הכחושים והשאר פטורין משום דלא נשתיירו אלא חמשה דלאו בר עישורי נינהו:
notes.en: He may not say: I will separate ten: the lean ones, and the rest are exempt, because only five would remain, and those are not subject to tithing [being fewer than ten].

notes.he: כולן בין כחושים בין שמנים. ותרי מילי אשמועינן חדא דאינו יכול לברור הכחושים וחדא אע"ג דלא נשתיירו אלא חמשה לא מצי למימר דליהוו פטורין לגמרי אלא מצטרפין לגורן אחר. וכמדומה דלא איצטריך למימר דהא אמרינן לעיל (בכורות דף נז:) דחמשה לפני הגורן וחמשה לאחר הגורן מצטרפין לעשרה אלא הכי פירושו לא יאמר וכו' והשאר ליהוו פטורין עכשיו שלא אכניסם בדיר עם האחרים ואע"פ שהגיע הגורן אוכל למכרן ולשוחטם הואיל ולאו בני עשורי נינהו דאין הגורן קובע אלא דבר הראוי למעשר והנך חמשה לאו בני עשורי נינהו אלא כונסן לדיר כולן ביחד ומוציא עשרה והשאר מצטרפין לגורן אחר על כרחו שהוקבע בדיר למעשר ולא יוכל למכור ולשוחטם:
notes.en: Rather, he brings them into the pen: all of them, lean and fat alike. Two things are taught here: first, that he cannot pick out the lean ones; second, that although only five remain, he cannot say they are entirely exempt; rather, they combine with another gathering time. It seems to me that this did not need to be said, since we said above (57b) that five before the gathering time and five after it combine to make ten. Rather, this is its meaning: he may not say, etc., “and let the rest be exempt now,” meaning: I will not bring them into the pen with the others, and although the gathering time has arrived I may sell them and slaughter them, since they are not subject to tithing, as the gathering time fixes [the obligation] only for something fit to be tithed, and these five are not. Rather, he brings them all into the pen together and takes out ten, and the rest combine with another gathering time perforce, since they were fixed for tithe in the pen, and he may not sell or slaughter them.

notes.he: מלצרפן אע"ג דהכניסן כולן לדיר:
notes.en: And the rest are exempt: from being combined [with a later gathering], even though he brought them all into the pen.

messages.text: But isn’t it taught in a baraita:
messages.quote: And the remainder combine with animals born later

messages.text: If one has nineteen lambs he may not say: I will separate ten and bring them into the pen, and I will take one of them as animal tithe and the rest will be exempt; rather, he must bring them all into the pen and remove ten of them by causing them to emerge from the opening, and take one of them, the tenth one, and the remainder are exempt.
According to this baraita, the remainder are not combined with animals born later.

We are dealing with a pen that has two openings. And nine of the lambs emerged through this opening and nine of them went out through that opening, and this last one remaining in the pen is fit to come out here or to come out there. Therefore, all the lambs emerged as part of a tally fit to reach ten.
messages.lead: Rav Huna bar Seḥora interpreted the baraita before Rava at the time of the Festival discourse:

notes.he: בשבת שלפני הרגל שבו דורשים הלכות הרגל:
notes.en: At the Festival: on the Shabbat before the Festival, when the laws of the Festival are expounded.

notes.he: שנשתייר באחרונה הוי מנין הראוי בין להכא ובין להכא ופוטר את כולן והוא עצמו קדוש הוי בין שיצא בין שנשתייר באחרונה דעשירי קדוש מאליו:
notes.en: And this one: which remained last makes a tally fit [to reach ten] both here and there, and exempts them all; and it itself is sacred, whether it went out or remained last, since the tenth is sanctified of its own accord.

notes.he: בשבת שלפני הרגל שדורשין בו. דהאי חד דנשתייר בדיר הי"ט חזי להשלים להכא ולהכא ואמרינן דספק מנין הראוי פטורין. ולישני ליה. אפילו בדיר של פתח אחד וכגון דמנה ט' וכי מטא י' קרא ההוא י' חד מרישא ומני עד עשרה דהשתא נפקו בין ט' ראשון בין ט' אחרון במנין הראוי:
notes.en: At the Festival: on the Shabbat before the Festival, when they expound. For this one, the nineteenth, that remained in the pen, is fit to complete [the tally] here and there, and we say that [animals that went out in] a tally possibly fit [to reach ten] are exempt. And let him answer: even in a pen with one opening, where he counted nine, and when the tenth arrived he called that tenth one, from the start, and counted up to ten; now both the first nine and the last nine went out in a fit tally.

messages.text: But let him teach instead that the baraita is referring to a case where he counted nine, and when the tenth lamb arrived to be counted he called it number one and began counting again from the start. In such a case he designated only the nineteenth lamb that emerged as number ten, and therefore all the other lambs are exempt.
messages.quote: a pen that has two openings

notes.he: שלא קראו עשירי אלא התחיל למנות כבתחלה אחד שנים שלשה ונמצא דהתשעה עשר היה עשירי ואפילו התשעה שמנה מתחלה נפטרו במנין הראוי:
notes.en: He called one from the start: he did not call it tenth but began counting again as at first, one, two, three; so the nineteenth turns out to be the tenth, and even the nine he counted at first were exempted by a tally fit [to reach ten].

messages.text: Rav Huna bar Seḥora holds that the tenth animal to come out of the pen is sanctified of its own accord, even if it was designated as number one.

notes.he: אע"פ שקראו אחד ונמצא שהתשעה אחרונים לא יהו פטורין:
notes.en: Of its own accord it is sacred: even though he called it one; so the last nine would not be exempt.

notes.he: רב הונא משום הכי ליכא לתרוצא הכי משום דהוי עשירי שקראו אחד לא כלום עבד דעשירי מאליו קדוש למעשר אפילו שלא קראו עשירי והנך ט' דמשתיירו לית בהו מנין הראוי וצריכי לאיצטרופי לגורן אחד אבל בב' פתחים דט' נפקי מהכא וט' מהכא וא' נשתייר ודאי ראוי להשלים הכא והכא:
notes.en: He holds: Rav Huna; that is why he could not answer that way, because [by calling the tenth one] he did nothing, since the tenth is sanctified as tithe of its own accord even if he did not call it tenth, and the nine that remain have no fit tally and must combine with another gathering time. But with two openings, where nine go out here and nine there and one remains, it is certainly fit to complete [the tally] here and there.

messages.text: But let him teach instead that the baraita is referring to a case of a designated time for gathering the animals, and that the pen has only one opening, but he counted them pair by pair, i.e., he called the first pair number one, the second pair number two, and so on. In this manner, the nineteenth lamb would be designated as number ten and thereby exempt the others.

notes.he: שנים כאחד וזוג עשירי לא היה רק אחד ויפטרו כולן במנין הראוי דההוא חד בתרא חזיא להכא ולהכא:
notes.en: Pair by pair: two as one, and the tenth “pair” was only a single animal, so all of them would be exempted by a fit tally, since that last one is fit for here and for there.

notes.he: בחד פתח וכגון דמנאן זוגות זוגות שנים באחד עד שהגיע לט' הוו להו י"ח והוציא האחד שנשתייר וקראו עשירי לפטור הללו ט' והללו ט':
notes.en: And let him answer: with one opening, where he counted them pair by pair, two as one, until he reached nine, which are eighteen, and he took out the one that remained and called it tenth, to exempt these nine and those nine.

messages.text: Rav Huna bar Seḥora holds that the tenth according to the number of animals is sanctified, regardless of how he counts them. Accordingly, one of the fifth pair would be the tithed animal, and the remaining nine would not be considered part of a tally fit to reach ten.

notes.he: דלא אזלינן אחר פיו שאומר אחד שנים אלא אחר בהמות שהוציא וכיון שהוציא חמש זוגות שהן עשרה בהמות הוי חד מינייהו קדוש ואינך כולן דהוציא לאחר כן במאי ליפטרי הא לא הוי מנין הראוי:
notes.en: According to the number of animals: we do not follow what his mouth says, “one, two,” but the animals he took out. Once he has taken out five pairs, which are ten animals, one of them is sacred; and all those he takes out afterward, by what would they be exempt? They are not a tally fit [to reach ten].

notes.he: רב הונא:
notes.en: He holds: Rav Huna.

notes.he: ולא לחשבון המונה כלומר דלא אזלינן בתר מנין דידיה דמונן זוגות זוגות אלא כיון דנפקו ה' זוגות הרי י' בהמות והוי חד מנייהו קדוש ואידך ד' זוגות לית להו מנין הראוי ולא ליפטרו הלכך ליכא לשנויי הכי:
notes.en: The tenth according to the number of animals is sacred, and not according to the counter’s reckoning: that is, we do not follow his own count, counting them pair by pair; rather, once five pairs have gone out, those are ten animals and one of them is sacred, and the other four pairs have no fit tally and would not be exempt. Therefore one cannot answer that way.

messages.text: The mother of Rav Huna bar Seḥora merited to give birth to such a son, who explained the halakha before Rava at the time of the Festival discourse in accordance with Rava’s own halakha.

notes.dh: זכאי אימיה דרב הונא בר סחורה דאשנייה ליה לרבא כשמעתיה
notes.he: כלומר זכתה אמו של רב הונא בר סחורה שילדה בן כמותו שידע לתרץ לרבא שמועתו בתוך הדרשא ותרצה לו בשיטת שמועתו דהא דקאמר לעיל מנין הראוי פוטר והכי קא מתרץ רב הונא הכא דהא חד חזי להכא וחזי להכא:
notes.en: Fortunate is the mother of Rav Huna bar Seḥora, who explained it to Rava in line with his own teaching: that is, the mother of Rav Huna bar Seḥora merited to bear a son like him, who knew how to resolve Rava’s teaching in the middle of the discourse, and resolved it along the lines of Rava’s own teaching; for Rava said above that a tally fit [to reach ten] exempts, and this is how Rav Huna resolves it here: that one is fit for here and fit for there.

notes.dh: זכאי אימיה דרב הונא בר סחורה
notes.he: דאע"ג דלא הוה חכם כ"כ ותריץ לו הברייתא לרבא בריגלא לפני רבים וכיון כשתירצה לו כשמעתיה דרבא דאמר מנין הראוי פוטר:
notes.en: Fortunate is the mother of Rav Huna bar Seḥora: for although he was not so great a scholar, he resolved the baraita for Rava at the Festival before the public, and he aimed well when he resolved it in line with Rava’s own teaching, who said that a fit tally exempts.

messages.text: Mishna

If two animals emerged as one, one counts them as twos, i.e., as though they came out one after the other. If he mistakenly counted two of the animals at the beginning or in the middle of the ten as one, and then continued his count, the ninth and the tenth are flawed, as he called the tenth: Ninth, and he called the eleventh: Tenth.

notes.he: כלומר אותו שקרא הוא תשיעי דהיינו עשירי ואותו שקרא הוא עשירי דהיינו אחד עשר עומדים לקלקלה שהוא סבור על התשיעי שהוא חולין ועל העשירי שהוא מעשר ואם עשה כן ולא נמלך בב"ד הרי הן מקולקלין כדקתני סיפא קרא לעשירי תשיעי ולאחד עשר עשירי העשירי מעשר ואחד עשר קרב שלמים. פ"א הויין מקולקלין דלא חל עליהן קדושה ליקרב אלא נאכלין במומן דאע"ג דבעלמא אם קרא לעשירי תשיעי ולאחד עשר עשירי העשירי קרב מעשר והאחד עשר קרב שלמים כדלקמן הני מילי היכא דלא טעה אלא מתשיעי ואילך אבל הכא כל המנין למעלה מתשיעי דקרא לשמיני שביעי ולשביעי ששי או לתשיעי שמיני לא הוו עשירי ואחד עשר קדושים ליקרב הואיל וטעה כל כך והא דקתני יצאו שנים כאחת לא מיירי מתשיעי ועשירי דהא מתשיעי ואילך קמפרש רבא דינא בגמרא אלא הכא מיירי כגון דטעה בחשבון מתשיעי ולמעלה כגון שיצאו שנים בשמיני וקראן שמיני אי נמי יצאו שנים בשביעי וקראן שביעי והא דקתני לקמן מנאן למפרע העשירי קדוש ההוא כדמפרש טעמא דמייתי לה במנינא דפרסאי דקרו לעשרה חדא. ואית דמפרשי משום הכי מקולקלין דמיירי כגון דנתכוין למנותן אחד ובמס' נזירות בפ' ב"ש (נזיר דף לב.) אמרינן גבי מעשר טעותו ולא כוונתו ולא נהירא משום דא"כ אפי' קרא לתשיעי עשירי נמי ליהוי מקולקל בלא יצאו שנים כאחת ועוד למאן דפליג התם דאמר טעותו ואפי' כוונתו מאי איכא למימר. ובנמוקי ר' מצאתי דמקולקלין היינו דקדושה חלה עליהן ומספקא ליה אמאי נקט לשון מקולקלין והכי נהירא טפי ואיכא למימר דפרושי קמפרש במשנה עצמה מ"ט מקולקלין משום דקרא לתשיעי עשירי וכו':
notes.en: MISHNA. The ninth and tenth are flawed: that is, the one he called ninth, which is really the tenth, and the one he called tenth, which is really the eleventh, stand to be spoiled, because he thinks the [so-called] ninth is non-sacred and the [so-called] tenth is the tithe; and if he acted so without consulting the court, they are spoiled. [The correct ruling is] as the latter clause teaches: if he called the tenth ninth and the eleventh tenth, the tenth is tithe and the eleventh is sacrificed as a peace offering. Another explanation: they are flawed because no sanctity takes hold of them to be sacrificed, and they are eaten in their blemished state. For although elsewhere, if he called the tenth ninth and the eleventh tenth, the tenth is sacrificed as tithe and the eleventh as a peace offering, as below, that applies only where he erred from the ninth onward; but here the whole count above the ninth is wrong, for he called the eighth seventh and the seventh sixth, or the ninth eighth, so the tenth and eleventh are not sacred to be sacrificed, since he erred so much. And when the mishna teaches “two emerged as one,” it is not speaking of the ninth and tenth, since Rava sets out the law from the ninth onward in the Gemara (60b); rather it speaks of one who erred in the count before the ninth, for example two emerged at the eighth and he called them eighth, or two emerged at the seventh and he called them seventh. And what is taught below, “if he counted them backward, the tenth is sacred,” is for the reason given there, citing the Persian counting, which calls ten “one.” Some explain that they are flawed because the case is where he intended to count them as one; and in tractate Nazir, in the chapter Beit Shammai (Nazir 32a), we say regarding tithe: his mistake [sanctifies], but not his intention. But this is not convincing: for if so, even if he called the ninth tenth it should be flawed, without two emerging as one; and further, according to the one who disputes there and says “his mistake, and even his intention,” what can be said? And in my teacher’s notes I found that “flawed” means that sanctity takes hold of them, and he was unsure why the mishna used the word “flawed.” This is more convincing, and one can say that the mishna itself explains why they are flawed: because he called the ninth tenth, etc.

notes.dh: יצאו שנים כאחד מונה אותן שנים ואם מנאן אחד תשיעי ועשירי מקולקלין
notes.he: פ"ה כגון שיצאו שנים כשהגיע לששה או לשבעה ומנאן אחד ועל כן קרא העשירי למנין בהמות תשיעי והאחד עשר עשירי אע"ג דבסמוך אמר קרא לעשירי תשיעי ולאחד עשר עשירי עשירי מעשר ואחד עשר שלמים הכא מקולקלין משום דמנה אחד בשנים שיצאו כאחד ומספקא לן אם נעשין כאחד ע"י שמנאן אחד או לא ואע"ג דאיכא מ"ד בגמרא עשירי למעשר בהמות קדוש דמה שמנאן אחד משוי ליה ספיקא ואותו הקרוי תשיעי הוי ספק תשיעי ספק עשירי והקרוי עשירי הוי ספק עשירי ספק קדוש ליקרב:
notes.en: If two emerged as one, he counts them as two, and if he counted them as one, the ninth and tenth are flawed: Rashi explained: for example, two emerged when he reached six or seven and he counted them as one, and therefore he called the tenth, by the number of animals, ninth, and the eleventh tenth. Although just below it says that if he called the tenth ninth and the eleventh tenth, the tenth is tithe and the eleventh a peace offering, here they are flawed because he counted the two that emerged together as one, and we are unsure whether they become as one by his counting them as one or not. And although there is an opinion in the Gemara that the tenth according to the number of animals is sacred, the fact that he counted them as one makes it a doubt: the one called ninth is perhaps the ninth, perhaps the tenth, and the one called tenth is perhaps the tenth, perhaps [the eleventh,] sacred to be sacrificed.

notes.he: לאותן שנים התשיעי והעשירי מקולקלין דתשיעי הוי עשירי ועשירי הוי אחד עשר ושלמים ומעשר מעורבין זה בזה ואין נאכלין במומן דשלמים אית מנייהו חזה ושוק לכהנים ומעשר אין ממנו חזה ושוק לכהנים אלא אימורין למזבח ואי יהיב מיניה חזה ושוק לכהנים קא מייתי קדשים לבית הפסול דשמא כהנים לא היו מנויין לאוכלו מפני שיש להן קדשים אחרים ומשיירין אותו חוץ לזמנו ונמצאו באין לבית הפסול דהא חזה ושוק דמעשר ודאי מותר לישראל הלכך לית להו תקנה אלא שניהם ירעו עד שיסתאבו ויפדה האחד של שלמים במעות ואחר כך נאכלין כולן לישראל:
notes.en: He counted them as one, those two: the ninth and tenth are flawed, for the [so-called] ninth is the tenth and the [so-called] tenth is the eleventh, a peace offering, and peace offering and tithe are intermingled with each other, and they are not eaten [except] in their blemished state. For from a peace offering the breast and thigh go to the priests, while from the tithe there is no breast and thigh for the priests, only the sacrificial portions for the altar. If he gives breast and thigh from it to the priests, he brings sacrificial animals to disqualification, for perhaps the priests would not be counted to eat it, since they have other offerings, and they would leave it beyond its time, and so it comes to disqualification, whereas the breast and thigh of a tithe are certainly permitted to an Israelite. Therefore they have no remedy except that both graze until they become blemished, and the one that is the peace offering is redeemed with money, and afterward they are all eaten by Israelites.

messages.text: If he mistakenly called the ninth: Tenth, and the tenth: Ninth, and the eleventh: Tenth, the three of them are sacred, although each has a different halakhic status. The ninth is eaten in its blemished state; and the tenth is animal tithe, which is sacrificed in the Temple and eaten by its owner; and the eleventh is sacrificed as a peace offering, from which the breast and the thigh are given to the priest.

notes.he: בגמ' מפיק מקרא:
notes.en: Is sacrificed as a peace offering: in the Gemara it is derived from a verse.

notes.he: כשיפול בו מום הואיל וקראו שם מעשר ומעשר גמור לא הוי להקרבה דהא תשיעי הוא אלא נאכל במומו:
notes.en: The ninth is eaten in its blemished state: when it develops a blemish, since he called it by the name tithe; but it is not a full tithe, fit to be sacrificed, since it is the ninth; rather it is eaten in its blemished state.

notes.he: וחזי להקרבה אע"ג דקראו ט' די' ודאי מאליו הוא קדוש:
notes.en: And the tenth is tithe, and is fit to be sacrificed, even though he called it ninth, for the tenth is certainly sacred of its own accord.

messages.text: And the eleventh renders a non-sacred animal that is exchanged for the peace offering consecrated as a substitute and he sacrifices it as a peace offering; this is the statement of Rabbi Meir.

notes.he: דמאחר דקדש י' ודאי הוי האיך שלמים ועוד מש"ה קדיש האי י"א דכיון דנעקר שם י' מי' ונקרא ט' וי"א נקרא י' מש"ה תפיס בו קדושת שלמים מאחר שקדש עשירי ודאי ועושה תמורה שאם המיר בהמה אחרת באותו אחד עשר הוי נתפס בתמורה:
notes.en: And the eleventh is sacrificed as a peace offering: since the tenth is certainly sacred, that one is a peace offering. Further, this eleventh is sacred for this reason: since the name tenth was removed from the tenth, which was called ninth, and the eleventh was called tenth, therefore the sanctity of a peace offering takes hold of it, once the tenth is certainly sacred. And it renders a substitute: if he exchanged another animal for that eleventh, it is caught up as a substitute.

messages.text: The eleventh animal itself, which he called tenth, is a substitute for animal tithe, and does a substitute render another animal a substitute? Everyone agrees that a substitute is created only in exchange for an originally consecrated animal.
messages.quote: And the eleventh renders a substitute

notes.he: דאחד עשר שקראו עשירי היינו תמורת מעשר ובמס' תמורה (דף יג.) גמרינן דאין תמורה עושה תמורה משום דכתיב תמורתו ולא תמורת תמורתו:
notes.en: And is there a substitute [that renders a substitute]? For the eleventh, which he called tenth, is the substitute of the tithe, and in tractate Temura (13a) we derive that a substitute does not render a substitute, as it is written “its substitute,” and not the substitute of its substitute.

notes.he: כלומר האי י"א גופיה הוי תמורת מעשר כדקאמר בגמ' טעות מעשר תמורה הוי (או תמורה) והיאך עושה תמורה והלא אין ממירין וחוזרין וממירין:
notes.en: And does a substitute render a substitute? That is, this eleventh is itself the substitute of the tithe, as the Gemara says (60b): a mistake in tithe is a substitute; so how can it render a substitute? Is it not so that one does not substitute and then substitute again?

messages.text: The eleventh animal is not considered a substitute for the animal tithe, since if it were a substitute it would not be sacrificed, as the substitute for an animal tithe is not sacrificed.

notes.he: אותו אחד עשר לא היה קרב דתמורת מעשר אינה קריבה כדגמרינן במס' תמורה (דף ה:) [מעשר העברה העברה מבכור ובבכור דרשינן הם קריבין ואין תמורתו קריבה] אלא ודאי מדקרב שלמים הקדש ראשון חשבינן ליה ולכך עושה תמורה כדין שלמים אחרים:
notes.en: If it were a substitute: that eleventh would not be sacrificed, since the substitute of a tithe is not sacrificed, as we derive in tractate Temura (5b) [tithe from the firstborn, through the shared word “passing”; and of the firstborn we expound: they are sacrificed, but their substitute is not]. Rather, certainly, since it is sacrificed as a peace offering, we regard it as an originally consecrated animal, and therefore it renders a substitute like any other peace offering.

notes.dh: אמרי משום ר' מאיר אילו היה תמורה לא היה קרב
notes.he: כלומר ודאי דאין תמורה עושה תמורה והכא האי אחד עשר לאו תמורה היא דלא הויא כשאר תמורה אלא שם מעשר איקרי עליה ולהכי קרבה אבל אי הויא תמורת הגוף של מעשר כדרך שאר תמורות לא הות קרבה דהא גרסינן בפרק ראשון של מסכת תמורה תנו רבנן לא יבקר כו' עד רבי אומר למה יצא מעשר מעתה לדונו בתמורת שמו ובתמורת גופו לומר לך תמורת שמו קרבה תמורת גופו לא קרבה. והאי אחד עשר תמורת שמו היא ולהכי קרבה ולהכי עושה תמורה דליתה כשאר תמורה דשאר תמורה תמורת הגוף הויא:
notes.en: They said in the name of Rabbi Meir: if it were a substitute it would not be sacrificed. That is, certainly a substitute does not render a substitute; but here this eleventh is not a substitute, as it is not like other substitutes; rather, the name tithe was called upon it, and so it is sacrificed. If it were a substitute of the body of the tithe, in the manner of other substitutes, it would not be sacrificed; for we read in the first chapter of tractate Temura: “The Sages taught: ‘He shall not inquire’ …” until “Rabbi says: Why was tithe singled out? To judge it with regard to the substitute of its name and the substitute of its body, to tell you that the substitute of its name is sacrificed and the substitute of its body is not.” And this eleventh is a substitute of its name, and therefore it is sacrificed and renders a substitute, for it is not like other substitutes, which are substitutes of the body.

messages.text: If one called the ninth animal: Tenth, and the tenth: Tenth, and the eleventh: Tenth, the eleventh is not consecrated. This is the principle: In any situation where the name of the tenth was not removed from the tenth animal, the eleventh that was called the tenth is not consecrated.

notes.he: מן הי' עצמו:
notes.en: From it: from the tenth itself.

messages.caption: The mishna’s two miscounts: what becomes of the ninth, tenth and eleventh when each is called by the wrong number.

messages.text: Gemara

If one counted the animals pair by pair, i.e., he called the first pair: One, and the second pair: Two, and so on, or if one counted them hundred [kinteran] by hundred, the tenth according to his number is sanctified.

notes.he: למאות שמנה כל מאה ומאה ביחד:
notes.en: Kinteran: by hundreds, counting each hundred together.

notes.he: וכשהגיע לזוג י' נטל ב' למעשר:
notes.en: He counted them pair by pair, and when he reached the tenth pair he took the two as tithe.

notes.he: קינטרין שמונה מאה ונוטל י' ממאה:
notes.en: Kinteran: he counts by the hundred and takes ten out of a hundred.

messages.text: When Rabbi Yoḥanan says that the tenth is sanctified according to his number, what does he mean?
messages.quote: the tenth according to his number is sanctified

messages.text: It is sanctified according to his counting, i.e., all the animals in whichever pair or group he calls: Ten, are sanctified, e.g., the tenth pair, which consists of the nineteenth and twentieth animals.

notes.he: מנין י' שהוא מונה שלאחר שמנה ט' מאות הוי הק' עשירית קודש:
notes.en: According to his number it is sacred: the count of ten that he is counting; once he has counted nine hundreds, the tenth hundred is sacred.

notes.he: כמו שהוא מונן:
notes.en: It is sacred according to his number: as he counts them.

messages.text: It is sanctified according to the number of animals, regardless of how he designates them.

notes.he: דלא אזלינן בתר מנין שלו אלא כשמנה ה' זוגות בהמות שהן י' בהמות הוי מיד מעשר בתר מנינו:
notes.en: According to the number of animals: we do not follow his own count; rather, once he has counted five pairs of animals, which are ten animals, [the tenth animal] is immediately tithe, by the animals’ count.

notes.he: למנין בהמות כדאמרן:
notes.en: According to the number of animals, as we said.

messages.text: In support of Rav Mari’s opinion: We learned in the mishna: If two animals emerged as one, one counts them as twos. If he mistakenly counted a pair of animals in the middle as one and continued his count, the ninth and the tenth are flawed, as he called the tenth: Ninth, and the eleventh: Tenth.
messages.quote: If two emerged as one, one counts them as twos

messages.text: Granted, according to the one who says: It is sanctified according to his counting, i.e., Rav Mari, it is due to that reason that the ninth and the tenth are flawed, because the number by which one designates them is significant, and he called the tenth animal the ninth, and the eleventh he designated as tenth.

But according to the one who says that the animal is sanctified according to the number of animals regardless of how the owner designates each one, i.e., Rav Kahana, why are they flawed? It should be considered as though he called the ninth animal the ninth, and the tenth animal he called: Tenth.

notes.he: האי קא קרי ליה לאו דוקא אלא כלומר אמאי מקולקלים הא אמרת דט' למנין בהמות הוי ט' וי' הוי עשירי דלא חיישינן למנין שלו וכיון דלא חיישינן אחד עשר שהוא קורא עשירי ועשירי שהוא קורא תשיעי אמאי מקולקלין ליהוי אחד עשר שלמים ועשירי מעשר:
notes.en: And the tenth he calls tenth: this “he calls it” is not meant literally; rather it means: why are they flawed? You said that the ninth by the number of animals is the ninth and the tenth is the tenth, since we pay no attention to his own count; and since we pay no attention to it, why should the eleventh, which he calls tenth, and the tenth, which he calls ninth, be flawed? Let the eleventh be a peace offering and the tenth tithe.

notes.he: אלא למאן דאמר למנין בהמות קדוש אמאי מקולקלין א"כ הוה ליה כאילו קרא לודאי תשיעי תשיעי ולודאי עשירי עשירי:
notes.en: But according to the one who says it is sacred according to the number of animals, why are they flawed? If so, it is as though he called the certain ninth ninth and the certain tenth tenth.

messages.text: According to Rav Kahana, Rabbi Yoḥanan could have said to you: When I said the designation goes according to the animal I was referring only to a case where he intended to take out the animals pair by pair, and he did not err. In such a case his designation is nullified and the animals are sanctified in accordance with the order they left the pen.

notes.he: ומתרץ אליבא דרב כהנא דכי אמינא למנין בהמות קדוש היכא דאיכוון לאפוקינהו כולהו זוגות זוגות או קינטרין אבל הכא במתני' דנפק ממילא דקתני יצאו שנים כאחד מעצמו לא קדוש למנין בהמה אלא למנין שלו:
notes.en: Rabbi Yoḥanan could say to you: he answers according to Rav Kahana: when I said it is sacred according to the number of animals, that is where he intended to take them all out pair by pair, or by hundreds; but here in the mishna, where it emerged by itself, as it teaches “two emerged as one” of their own accord, it is sacred not according to the number of animals but according to his own count.

messages.text: But with regard to a case where the animal emerged by itself and the owner miscounted I did not say the designation goes according to the number of the animal, as the Torah explicitly includes a case where the sanctification follows a mistaken designation (see 60b).

notes.he: אמרינן למנין בהמות קדוש אלא בתר מנין שלו נמי אזלינן:
notes.en: Where it emerged by itself, not: we do not say it is sacred according to the number of animals; rather we follow his own count too.

messages.text: Come and hear another proof from a baraita:
If one counted them backward, i.e., ten, nine, eight, and so on, the tenth animal in the numbering, which he designated as number one, is sanctified.

notes.he: שהראשון שיצא קרא עשרה והב' תשעה והג' שמנה וכן כולם עד אחד העשר שבמנין שקרא אחד הוי קדוש:
notes.en: He counted them backward: he called the first to go out ten, the second nine, the third eight, and so on for all of them down to one; the tenth in the count, which he called one, is sacred.

notes.he: שלראשון קרא י' לשני ט' עד א':
notes.en: He counted them backward: to the first he called ten, to the second nine, down to one.

messages.text: Granted, according to the one who says that the tithe is sanctified according to the number of animals regardless of how he designates each animal, i.e., Rav Kahana, this works out well, as the tenth animal is sanctified. But according to the one who says it is sanctified according to his counting, i.e., Rav Mari, why is the tenth animal sanctified? After all, he called the tenth animal number one.

The tenth animal is sanctified according to Rav Mari because it has been counted as number ten in Persian counting, as they call the tenth one in their language by the term one, i.e., they count only in units of ten, and call these units: One. Therefore, in this case there is no contradiction between the designation and the number of the animal.
messages.quote: he called the tenth animal number one

notes.he: דלעשרה קרו חד הוי האי חד כמו עשירי למנין שלו וקדוש שלשתן מקודשות ולא קא מיירי בנתערבו:
notes.en: Since it is in the Persian count, where they call ten “one,” this “one” is like the tenth by his own count, and is sacred. [The notes that follow] belong to the mishna, “the three of them are sacred,” which does not speak of animals that became intermingled.

messages.text: All three are sacred, although each has a different halakhic status. A relevant baraita: The Sages taught:
messages.quote: called the ninth: Tenth, and the tenth: Ninth, and the eleventh: Tenth

messages.text: From where is it derived that if one mistakenly called the ninth animal: Tenth, and the tenth animal: Ninth, and the eleventh animal: Tenth, that all three of them are sanctified?

The verse states: “And all the tithe of the herd or the flock, whatever passes under the rod, the tenth shall be sacred to the Lord”. This indicates that the tenth animal that passes under the rod is imbued with sanctity, in addition to any animal that the owner designates as the tenth. One might have thought that I include even the eighth animal or the twelfth animal, if they were mistakenly designated as the tenth.

verse.he: וְכׇל־מַעְשַׂר בָּקָר וָצֹאן כֹּל אֲשֶׁר־יַעֲבֹר תַּחַת הַשָּׁבֶט הָעֲשִׂירִי יִהְיֶה־קֹּדֶשׁ לַיהֹוָה׃
verse.en: All tithes of the herd or flock—of all that passes under the shepherd’s staff, every tenth one—shall be holy to GOD.

notes.he: משמע בין שקראו הוא עשירי בין שהיה עשירי למנין ולא קראו עשירי:
notes.en: And all the tithe of the herd or the flock: this implies both where he called it tenth and where it was tenth in the count and he did not call it tenth.

notes.he: אם קראם עשירי:
notes.en: Eighth and twelfth: if he called them tenth.

notes.he: לרבות כל שקרא עליו שם מעשר:
notes.en: And all the tithe: to include anything upon which he called the name tithe.

notes.he: אף שמיני ושנים עשר שאם קרא לשמיני מעשר ולשנים עשר:
notes.en: Even the eighth and twelfth: if he called the eighth tithe, and the twelfth.

messages.text: You said in response that since the tenth animal is sanctified and the animal that he designated by mistake as the tenth is sanctified, their statuses should be compared: Just as the tenth animal is sanctified only with an animal that was close to the number ten, i.e., it itself was the tenth, so too, an animal that was designated by mistake is sanctified only if it is close to the number ten, i.e., if it is the ninth or eleventh, but not if it is the eighth or the twelfth.

notes.he: העשירי גמור אינו מקודש אלא בסמוך לו שאין לך סמוך בו יותר מגופו:
notes.en: Just as it: the full tenth is sanctified only [when it is] close to it, for nothing is closer to it than itself.

notes.he: מה שהוא טעה וקרא עשירי אינו מקודש אא"כ שטעה באותו שסמוך למעשר גמור כגון תשיעי ואחד עשר שהן סמוכין לו זה מלפניו וזה מלאחריו:
notes.en: So too its mistake: the one about which he erred and called it tenth is sanctified only if he erred about one adjacent to the full tithe, such as the ninth and eleventh, which are adjacent to it, one before it and one after it.

notes.he: כגון כשקרא לתשיעי עשירי או לאחד עשר עשירי:
notes.en: And its mistake sanctifies: for example, when he called the ninth tenth or the eleventh tenth.

notes.dh: מה הוא אינו מקודש אלא בסמוך
notes.he: כלומר העשירי עצמו כשקורא אותו עשירי אין לך סמוך יותר מעצמו:
notes.en: Just as it is sanctified only [when] close: that is, the tenth itself, when he calls it tenth; there is nothing closer than itself.

notes.he: אף טעותו אינה מתקדש' אלא בסמוך לו לאפוקי שמיני ושנים עשר:
notes.en: So too its mistake is sanctified only [when] close to it: to exclude the eighth and twelfth.

messages.text: The mishna teaches that if one mistakenly designated the ninth and the eleventh animals as the tenth they are both sanctified. But isn’t it taught in a baraita:
messages.quote: the three of them are sacred

messages.text: Just as the tenth animal itself is unique, i.e., it is only one, so too, an animal that was designated by mistake is unique, i.e., only one additional animal receives the sanctity, but not both the ninth and the eleventh.

notes.he: שהעשירי אינו אלא אחד:
notes.en: Unique: for the tenth is only one.

notes.he: שאם טעה בתשיעי ובאחד עשר לא היו שנים מקודשין אלא אחד מהם והיכי אמרת דכולהו מקודשים:
notes.en: So too its mistake is unique: if he erred with the ninth and the eleventh, the two would not be sanctified, only one of them; so how did you say that all of them are sanctified?

notes.he: כלומר שאינו מקדש אלא אחת או תשיעי או אחד עשר ומותיב למתני' דקתני שלשתן מקודשין דהיינו ב' טעיות:
notes.en: So too its mistake is unique: that is, it sanctifies only one, either the ninth or the eleventh. And he raises an objection from the mishna, which teaches “the three of them are sacred,” which means two mistakes.

messages.text: A tanna taught before Rabbi Yoḥanan: In accordance with whose opinion is this baraita? It is in accordance with the opinion of Rabbi Elazar, son of Rabbi Shimon, as it is taught in a baraita:
messages.quote: so too, an animal that was designated by mistake is unique

notes.he: דבעי טעותו מיוחדת ר' אלעזר בר' שמעון דתניא לעולם כו':
notes.en: Whose is this? The one that requires its mistake to be unique: Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Shimon, as it is taught: “Never,” etc.

messages.text: The eleventh animal is never sanctified unless the owner is silent when the ninth animal leaves the pen, i.e., he does not designate it as the tenth, and he subsequently calls the tenth animal the ninth and the eleventh animal the tenth. But if he had already designated the ninth animal as the tenth, the eleventh cannot become sanctified.

notes.he: שאילו קראו עשירי לא ליהוי אחד עשר קדוש משום דשני טעיות של מעשר אחד אינן קדושים דטעותו מיוחדת כהוא עצמו:
notes.en: Until he is silent at the ninth: for if he had called it tenth, the eleventh would not be sacred, since two mistakes for one tithe are not sacred, as its mistake is unique, like itself.

notes.dh: עד שישתוק בתשיעי (אלא שלא קראו עשירי לה)
notes.he: יש לפרש בשני ענינים לאו דוקא שישתוק בתשיעי אלא שלא קראו עשירי ואפילו קראו תשיעי דאם קראו עשירי אין אחד עשר קדוש דשתי טעיות אין קדושין כאחד דטעות מיוחדת בעינן כהוא עצמו ועוד יש לפרש דאם קראו לתשיעי תשיעי תו לא הוי טעות כשקרא לעשירי תשיעי וכאילו קראו עשירי דמי ואין אחד עשר מקודש דלא חשיב כאילו נעקרה שם עשירי ממנו והשתא הוי שישתוק דוקא שלא ידבר כלל ומתרצא בהכי קושיא אחת לקמן בשמעתין דקאמר הב"ע דקדים חד מינייהו ואפיק לרישיה וקרא אחד עשר ומקשי עלה כמאן דלא כרבי דאי כרבי הא אמר אחד עשר לא הוי עקירה והשתא לוקמה דקרוי תשיעי לההוא דאפקיה לרישיה דלדברי הכל הויא עקירה ולפי פירוש זה ניחא דלא הוי עקירה כדפרי' וללשון ראשון שפירשתי להכי לא מוקי ליה דלקרייה תשיעי דלא איצטריך למיתני הא דודאי הוי עקירה אבל הא איצטריך לאשמועינן משום דזמנין לא הוי עקירה לרבי היכא דאית ליה בהמות טובא:
notes.en: Until he is silent at the ninth (that is, he did not call it tenth): this can be explained in two ways. [First:] “until he is silent at the ninth” is not meant literally; it means he did not call it tenth, even if he called it ninth. For if he called it tenth, the eleventh is not sacred, since two mistakes are not sanctified together, as we require that its mistake be unique, like itself. Or one can explain further: if he called the ninth “ninth,” then it is no longer a mistake when he calls the tenth “ninth,” and it is as though he called it tenth, and the eleventh is not sanctified, since it does not count as though the name tenth were removed from it. On this reading “he is silent” is literal: he did not speak at all. This resolves a difficulty further on in our passage, where it says: “Here we are dealing with a case where one of them went ahead and put out its head, and he called it eleventh,” and asks: “In accordance with whom? Not in accordance with Rabbi, for Rabbi said that [calling it] eleventh is not a removal.” Then let it be explained where he called the one that put out its head “ninth,” which according to all is a removal! According to this explanation it is well, since that is not a removal, as we explained. And according to the first version that I explained, it is not explained as a case where he called it ninth because that would not need to be taught, since it is certainly a removal; but this needed to be taught, because at times, according to Rabbi, it is not a removal, where he has many animals.

notes.he: שלא יקרא לו שם עשירי ויקרא לי' ט' ולי"א י' דליכא אלא טעות אחד דאחד עשר עשירי:
notes.en: Until he is silent at the ninth: so that he does not call it by the name tenth, and he calls the tenth ninth and the eleventh tenth, so that there is only one mistake, the eleventh [called] tenth.

notes.he: י' תשיעי לא הוי טעות משום דעשירי מאליו הוי קדוש וא"ת הם הכי נמי לימא שאם שתק בי"א ולא קראו י' לט' קראו י' ההוא ט' ליהוי קדוש הואיל והוי טעות מיוחדת הא לא קשיא בדין הוא די"א הוי קדוש הואיל וכבר קדש עשירי גופיה הוה ליה האי י"א תמורת שמו של מעשר ואיתפיס הוא בקדושה אבל ט' דאכתי לא קדש ליה מעשר גופיה היכי ליתפסיה לתשיעי לקדושי הואיל ואיהו גופיה אכתי לא הוי קדוש להכי נקט י"א ולא נקט ט':
notes.en: [Calling the] tenth “ninth” is not a mistake, since the tenth is sacred of its own accord. And if you ask: then let him say likewise that if he was silent at the eleventh and did not call it tenth, [but] called the ninth tenth, that ninth should be sacred, since it is a single mistake. This is no difficulty: by right the eleventh is sacred, since the tenth itself has already become sacred, so this eleventh is a substitute of the name of the tithe, and it is caught up in the sanctity. But the ninth, when the tithe itself has not yet become sacred, how could [the tithe] catch the ninth and sanctify it, when it itself is not yet sacred? Therefore he spoke of the eleventh and not the ninth.

messages.text: Rabbi Elazar, son of Rabbi Shimon, holds in accordance with the opinion of Rabbi Yehuda, who says: When the owner makes a mistake in designating animal tithe, e.g., if one designates the ninth animal as the tenth, the designated animal has the status of a substitute animal.

notes.he: וטעמא דרבי אלעזר הכי הוי משום דסבר לה כר' יהודה דאמר במתני' טעות וכו' דקאמר וכי יש תמורה עושה תמורה ור"ש אבוה דר' אלעזר אמר בפ' ראשון דתמורה (דף ט.) דאין ממירין וחוזרין וממירין דלאחר שהמירו על הבהמה פעם אחת אינה תופסת עוד תמורה פעם אחרת והכא נמי אין שתי טעיות למעשר:
notes.en: And the reason of Rabbi Elazar is this: because he holds like Rabbi Yehuda, who says in the mishna that a mistake [in tithe is a substitute], as he says, “and does a substitute render a substitute?”; and Rabbi Shimon, Rabbi Elazar’s father, said in the first chapter of Temura (9a) that one does not substitute and then substitute again: once a substitute has been made for the animal one time, it no longer takes a substitute another time. So too here, there are not two mistakes for one tithe.

messages.text: And Rabbi Elazar also holds in accordance with the opinion of his father, Rabbi Shimon, who says: One cannot effect substitution on one animal by substituting it for a specific offering, and again effect substitution, on another animal, by substituting it for the same offering, and if one attempts to do so the second animal does not become consecrated. Therefore, if one mistakenly called the ninth animal the tenth, that ninth animal has sanctity; but if he also calls the eleventh animal the tenth, this designation has no effect.

notes.he: וסבר לה ר' אלעזר כאבוה ר"ש דאמר בתמורה אין מימר חוזר ומימר דלאחר שהמיר בבהמת קדשים בהמה של חולין אינו חוזר ומימר בהמה אחרת של חולין באותה בהמה של קדשים:
notes.en: And Rabbi Elazar holds like his father, Rabbi Shimon, who says in Temura that one does not substitute and then substitute again: after he has substituted a non-sacred animal for a consecrated animal, he does not again substitute another non-sacred animal for that same consecrated animal.

notes.he: והכא נמי ט' וי"א אין ממירין בי' ומסתברא דהך מילתא אליבא דר' יוחנן היא דאמר התם כשם שאין ממירין שנים באחד כך אין ממירין וחוזרין וממירין:
notes.en: So too here, the ninth and the eleventh are not [both] substituted for the tenth. And it stands to reason that this follows Rabbi Yoḥanan, who said there: just as one does not substitute two for one, so one does not substitute and then substitute again.

messages.text: If two animals emerged from the pen together as the ninth, and he called them both the ninth, then the tenth, i.e., the tithe, and a non-sacred animal are considered intermingled with each other.

notes.he: כשהיה תשיעי ראוי לצאת:
notes.en: At the ninth: when the ninth was due to come out.

notes.he: דאחד מהן הוי תשיעי ואחד מעשר אע"ג דקראו תשיעי:
notes.en: Tenth and non-sacred: for one of them is the ninth and one is the tithe, although he called it ninth.

notes.he: ואין נאכלין אלא במומן והגוזז והעובד אחד מהן אינו סופג את הארבעים דשמא חולין הוא:
notes.en: Intermingled: and they are eaten only in their blemished state; and one who shears or works one of them does not receive the forty [lashes], since perhaps it is the non-sacred one.

notes.he: ושניהם יאכלו במומן לבעלים ולהכי קאמר עשירי וחולין מעורבין דאי עבד גיזה ועבודה בחד מינייהו או אכל חד מינייהו בלא מום או גאל או מכר אחד מהן הואיל ואית בהו חד חולין מספיקא לא מלקינן ליה הואיל ואית בהו חד חולין:
notes.en: The tenth and non-sacred are intermingled with each other: and both are eaten by the owners in their blemished state. That is why he says “tenth and non-sacred are intermingled”: if he shore or worked one of them, or ate one of them without a blemish, or redeemed or sold one of them, we do not flog him, out of doubt, since one of them is non-sacred.

messages.text: The tenth is sanctified of its own accord, despite the fact that he called it the ninth. And the animal that came out ninth is non-sacred, as it came out ninth and he called it the ninth. Since there is no way to determine which animal is which, neither of them can be brought as an offering, and they must both be left to graze until they develop a blemish.

notes.he: אף על פי שלא קראו עשירי:
notes.en: The tenth is sacred of its own accord: even though he did not call it tenth.

messages.text: If two animals emerged from the pen together as the ninth, and he called them both the tenth, then the tenth, i.e., the tithe, and the ninth animal, which he designated as the tenth, are intermingled with each other. What is the reason? He called both of them the tenth. The tenth has the sanctity of the tithe while the ninth was designated as the tenth, and therefore may not be eaten until it develops a blemish. Since there is no way to determine which animal is which, neither can be sacrificed, but they must both be left to graze until they develop a blemish.

notes.he: וכיון דיצאו שנים כאחד ולא ידע הי י' והי ט' לפיכך עשירי וט' מעורבין זה בזה. והוו להו תרוייהו קדושים ואי גאל ומכר אחד מהן לוקה דתרוייהו עשירי קרי להו ויאכלו במומן לבעלים:
notes.en: And the ninth he calls tenth: since two emerged as one and he does not know which is the tenth and which the ninth, the tenth and ninth are intermingled with each other, and both are sacred; if he redeemed or sold one of them he is flogged, since he called both of them tenth; and they are eaten by the owners in their blemished state.

messages.text: If two animals emerged from the pen together as the tenth, and he called them both the tenth, then the tenth, and the eleventh animal, which he designated as the tenth, are intermingled with each other.

notes.he: כלומר מעשר גמור ואחד עשר קדוש הויין מעורבין ביחד ומשום דאחד עשר שהוא קדוש קרב שלמים לכך יקרבו שניהם ויאכלו כחומר קודש שבהן דטעונין שתי מתנות והרמת חזה ושוק כמו שלמים:
notes.en: The tenth and eleventh are intermingled: that is, a full tithe and a sacred eleventh are intermingled together; and since the eleventh, which is sacred, is sacrificed as a peace offering, both are sacrificed and eaten according to the stricter of the two: they require two placements [of blood] and the lifting of the breast and thigh, like a peace offering.

notes.he: לעיל פ"ב (בכורות יז: ושם ד"ה אפשר) פירשתי דמצי סבר אי אפשר לצמצם:
notes.en: Two at the tenth, etc.: above, in chapter 2 (Bekhorot 17b, s.v. “efshar”), I explained that he could hold that it is impossible to be precise [so that two animals cannot emerge at exactly the same moment].

notes.dh: עשירי ואחד עשר מעורבין זה בזה
notes.he: דאחד עשר חזי להקרבת שלמים ואינך נאכל במומו לבעלים והשתא ליהוו תרווייהו רועין עד שיסתאבו והדר פודה חד מנייהו משום ההוא דשלמים וליהוו תרווייהו נאכלין במומן לבעלים:
notes.en: The tenth and eleventh are intermingled with each other: for the eleventh is fit to be sacrificed as a peace offering, and the other is eaten by the owners in its blemished state. So now both graze until they become blemished, then he redeems one of them on account of the peace offering, and both are eaten by the owners in their blemished state.

messages.text: If he called them both the eleventh, the tenth and a non-sacred animal are intermingled with each other.

notes.he: ותרויהו יאכלו במומן לבעלים בלא שום פדיון:
notes.en: The tenth and non-sacred are intermingled: and both are eaten by the owners in their blemished state, without any redemption.

messages.caption: Rava’s four cases: two animals come out together, at the ninth or at the tenth, and what each call leaves intermingled.

messages.text: Why do I need this additional case? This reasoning for the halakha in the case where the animals emerged together as the tenth is identical to that of the first case, where the animals emerged together as the ninth.
messages.quote: If two animals emerged from the pen together as the tenth, and he called them both the tenth

notes.he: כיון דאשמעינן דיצאו שניהם בתשיעי וקראן עשירי ממילא ידענא דכי ההיא דינא איכא ביצאו שניהם בעשירי:
notes.en: Why do I need this additional case? Since he taught us that two emerged at the ninth and he called them tenth, I would know by itself that the same law applies where both emerged at the tenth.

notes.he: עשירי ואחד עשר מעורבין היינו י' וט' מעורבין ומחדא שמעינן אידך:
notes.en: This is identical: “the tenth and eleventh are intermingled” is the same as “the tenth and ninth are intermingled,” and from one we learn the other.

messages.text: This latter clause teaches us that in every case where two animals emerge as one they are both sanctified, and this is the halakha even though the name of the tenth was not removed from the tenth animal. This situation is not included in the principle of the mishna: In any situation where the name of the tenth was not removed from the tenth animal, the eleventh that was called tenth is not consecrated.

notes.he: הא י' וי"א מעורבין דכל בבת אחת כי נפקי בבת אחת וקראו עשירי תרווייהו קדשי והוו חד קרב שלמים אע"ג דלא נעקר שם עשירי מעשירי דקראו עשירי:
notes.en: This teaches us: this, “the tenth and eleventh are intermingled,” [teaches] that whenever they emerge at the same time and he called them tenth, both are sacred, and one is sacrificed as a peace offering, even though the name tenth was not removed from the tenth, since he called it tenth.

messages.text: Rav Kahana sat and recited this halakha.

@Rav Kahana But the name of the tenth has not been removed from it. And didn’t we learn in the mishna that this is the principle: In any situation where the name of the tenth was not removed from the tenth animal, the eleventh that was called tenth is not consecrated?

@Rav Ashi This statement, that the designation of tenth must be removed, applies only when the animals leave the pen one after the other. But if two animals emerge from the pen at the same time, and he simultaneously designated the tenth and eleventh as tithe, both of them are sanctified.
messages.quote: But the name of the tenth has not been removed from it

notes.he: דקרא שם עשירי לעשירי ולאחד עשר בב"א אע"ג דלא נעקרה דהא לעשירי נמי קרא עשירי:
notes.en: At the same time: where he called the name tenth upon the tenth and the eleventh at the same time, even though it was not removed, since he called the tenth too “tenth.”

notes.he: דבעינן דליתעקר שם עשירי ממנו לכי נפקי בזה אחר זה דכיון דקרא לעשירי ודאי עשירי לא קדש אחד עשר:
notes.en: This statement, that we require the name tenth to be removed from it, applies when they emerge one after the other, for once he has called the certain tenth “tenth,” the eleventh is not sacred.

notes.he: כי נפקי בחדא וקראו עשירי תרוייהו קדש:
notes.en: But at the same time: when they emerge together and he called both of them tenth, [the eleventh] is sacred.

messages.text: How can the mishna be explained as referring only to a case where the animals left the pen one after the other? After all, the mishna teaches explicitly: If one called the ninth animal: Tenth, and the tenth: Tenth, and the eleventh: Tenth, the eleventh is not consecrated. This is the principle: In any situation where the name of the tenth was not removed from the tenth animal, the eleventh that was called tenth is not consecrated.

What does the phrase: This is the principle, serve to include? Does it not serve to include a case where the tenth and eleventh animals leave the pen at the same time? And if so, it is teaching that in such a case the eleventh animal is not sanctified.

notes.he: דלא קדש נמי י"א:
notes.en: Is it not to include at the same time? That the eleventh is not sacred then either.

messages.text: Rav Kahana would answer: No; it serves not to include that case, but to include a situation where the tenth animal emerged from the pen and the owner did not speak at all, and when the eleventh animal came out he designated it as the tenth. Therefore, the eleventh animal is not sanctified, as he did not remove the name of the tenth from the tenth animal. But if the tenth and eleventh animals came out at the same time, and he designated them both as the tenth, they are both sanctified.

notes.he: דלא חשיבא עקירה בהך שתיקה אא"כ עקרו בפירוש וקראו תשיעי:
notes.en: To include where the tenth emerged and he did not speak: for this silence does not count as removal unless he removed it explicitly and called it ninth.

notes.dh: לא לאיתויי יצא עשירי לבדו ולא דיבר
notes.he: שלא קראו י' ואח"כ יצא אחד עשר וקראו עשירי ואינו מקודש אחד עשר דהא לא (נפקי) [נפיק] שם העשירי ממנו דעשירי מאליו הוא קדוש אבל בב"א תרוייהו קדשי:
notes.en: No, to include where the tenth emerged alone and he did not speak: he did not call it tenth, and afterward the eleventh emerged and he called it tenth; the eleventh is not sanctified, since the name tenth did not leave [the tenth], for the tenth is sacred of its own accord. But at the same time, both are sacred.

messages.text: This must be the case, because if you do not say this explanation of the mishna there is a problem with that which is taught in a baraita:

notes.he: דבב"א קדוש. ולרב אשי דקפריך לרב כהנא והלא לא נעקר וכו' לא הוה שמיע ליה מה דתריצנא לעיל הא קמ"ל דבב"א כו':
notes.en: Because if you do not say this: that at the same time it is sacred. And Rav Ashi, who challenged Rav Kahana, “But [the name] has not been removed,” etc., had not heard what we answered above: “This teaches us that [in every case where two emerge] at the same time,” etc.

messages.text: If two animals emerged from the pen together as the tenth, and one did not come out before the other, and he called them both the tenth, the tenth and eleventh animals are intermingled with each other.

One is sacred with the sanctity of the animal tithe while the other is a peace offering, but there is no way to determine which animal is which. How can this baraita be reconciled with the mishna? He did not remove the name of the tenth from the tenth animal. Rather, is it not due to the fact that we say: In any case where two animals come out of the pen at the same time both of them are sanctified?
messages.quote: the tenth and eleventh animals are intermingled with each other

messages.text: Rav Ashi would rebut this claim: If it is due to that reason there is no conclusive argument. Here we are dealing with a case where one of the two animals came out before the other and brought its head out from the pen, and the owner called that animal the eleventh, and afterward it became intermingled with the other animals, and the last two animals came out together, and he called them both the tenth animal.

notes.he: דקתני עשירי ואחד עשר מעורבין דחשבינן ליה לאחד עשר מקודש אע"ג דקרא לעשירי עשירי כגון דקדים כו':
notes.en: Here we are dealing with: [the baraita] that teaches “the tenth and eleventh are intermingled,” where we regard the eleventh as consecrated even though he called the tenth “tenth”: for example, where one went ahead, etc.

notes.dh: דאי לא תימא הכי דתנן וכו'
notes.he: דקדים חד מנייהו ואפקיה לרישיה וקרייה אחד עשר. קמי דליקרא עשירי דהא נעקר שם עשירי מעשירי:
notes.en: Because if you do not say this, that which is taught, etc.: where one of them went ahead and put out its head and he called it eleventh before he called [anything] tenth, for then the name tenth was removed from the tenth.

messages.text: In such a case both animals are sanctified, as the name of the tenth was removed from the tenth animal when he mistakenly called it the eleventh animal.

notes.he: דהשתא נעקר שם עשירי ממנו שלא קראו עשירי אלא אחד עשר ולהכי אע"ג דהדר קרא אתרוייהו עשירי קדוש האחד עשר אבל היכא דמתחלה קרינהו עשירי אע"ג דבבת אחת לא הוי אחד עשר קדוש ולהכי מוקמינן כגון דקרייה אחד עשר דאי קרייה תשיעי לא איצטריך למיתני דהא ודאי עקירה הוי אבל באחד עשר פליג רבי ואמר דלא הוי עקירה כדלקמן ואיצטריך לאשמועינן דהוי עקירה:
notes.en: And called it eleventh: now the name tenth has been removed from it, since he did not call it tenth but eleventh; therefore, even though he then called both of them tenth, the eleventh is sacred. But where he had called it tenth at first, the eleventh would not be sacred, even at the same time. And we explain it as a case where he called it eleventh because, had he called it ninth, there would be no need to teach it, since that is certainly a removal; but regarding “eleventh,” Rabbi disagrees and says it is not a removal, as below, and it was necessary to teach us that it is a removal.

messages.text: How can one interpret the baraita as referring to a case where one animal put its head out before the other? But isn’t it taught explicitly in the baraita: And one did not come out before the other?
messages.quote: and one did not come out before the other

messages.text: What does the baraita mean when it states: And one did not come out before the other? It means that it did not come out completely, but returned and became intermingled with the other animals.

notes.he: והדר איערוב ובשעת יציאתם ממש לא קדם אחד את חברו:
notes.en: And then it became intermingled, and at the moment of their actual emergence, neither went ahead of the other.

messages.text: And in accordance with whose opinion is this baraita taught? It is not taught in accordance with the opinion of Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi. As, if it reflects the opinion of Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi there is a difficulty. Doesn’t Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi say: If one called the tenth animal the eleventh, it is not considered a removal of the name of the tenth from the tenth animal?

notes.he: מתרצינן דמה שקורא אחד עשר חשיבא עקירה:
notes.en: And in accordance with whom: is our answer, that calling it eleventh counts as removal?

notes.he: קא חשיב האי עקירה היכא דקראו אחד עשר דלא כרבי:
notes.en: And in accordance with whom: does he count this as removal, where he called it eleventh? Not in accordance with Rabbi.

messages.text: You may even say that the baraita is in accordance with the opinion of Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi, as when Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi said his statement he was referring only to a case where the owner has many animals to tithe. The reason is that we say that when he said: Aḥad asar, eleventh, his intention was to say: Ḥad issura, one group of ten, i.e., that this tenth animal completes one set of ten animals, not that it is the eleventh.

notes.he: לעשר דהשתא כי מנה עשרה ראשונים וקרא העשירי אחד עשר איכא למימר דבהכי לא נעקר שם עשירי ממנו דמאי אחד עשר דקאמר חד עישורא קאמר כלו' זה עישור ראשון:
notes.en: Where he has many animals: to tithe; now, when he counted the first ten and called the tenth “eleventh,” one can say that the name tenth was not removed from it by this, for what he meant by “eleventh [aḥad asar]” was “one tithe [ḥad issura],” that is, this is the first tithe.

notes.he: לעשורי דודאי כי קרי לעשירי אחד עשר לאו אחד עשר ממש הוא דקאמר אלא עשירי הוא דקרי ליה:
notes.en: Where he has many animals: to tithe; for certainly when he calls the tenth “eleventh” he does not really mean eleventh, but he is calling it tenth.

notes.he: כלומר הרי כבר מניתי אחד עשרון וכבר הפרשתי מעשר אחד מן המעשרות שיש לי להפריש:
notes.en: And he meant “one tithe”: that is, I have already counted one set of ten and have already separated one tithe of the tithes I must separate.

messages.text: Here it is referring to a situation where he does not have many animals to tithe, and therefore he could not have been speaking of more than one set of ten, in which case Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi agrees that calling it the eleventh removes its status as the tenth.

notes.he: מאחד עשר או י"ב או י"ג או י"ד או ט"ו ליכא למימר הכי שאין מנהגו של עולם לומר זה עישור אחד אלא אם כן יודע שיהו לו עישוריות הרבה הלכך אמרינן דאחד עשר ממש קאמר ועקר שם עשירי ממנו:
notes.en: But where he does not have more animals: than eleven, or twelve, or thirteen, or fourteen, or fifteen, one cannot say so, for it is not the way of the world to say “this is one tithe” unless one knows he will have many tithes. Therefore we say he really meant eleventh, and he removed the name tenth from it.

notes.he: היכא דלית ליה בהמות טובא אלא או [תשעה] עשר או ט"ו ודאי כי קרי לי' אחד עשר אפי' רבי מודה דהוי עקירת שם עשירי ממנו. וליתא לדרבא דאמר בב"א תרווייהו קדשי:
notes.en: Where he does not have many animals, only [nine]teen or fifteen: certainly when he calls it eleventh, even Rabbi agrees that this is a removal of the name tenth from it. And Rava’s statement, that at the same time both are sacred, does not stand.

messages.text: To what statement of Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi is the Gemara referring? As it is taught in a baraita:
If one called the tenth animal the eleventh and the eleventh animal the tenth, the eleventh animal is not sanctified; this is the statement of Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi.
The eleventh animal is sanctified.
messages.quote: the eleventh animal is not sanctified

messages.text: As long as the name of the tenth has not been removed from the tenth animal, the eleventh animal is not sanctified.
Here we are dealing with a case where he has many animals, and the reason is that we say that when he said: Aḥad asar, his intention was to say: Ḥad issura.
messages.lead: To clarify why the eleventh animal is not sanctified according to Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi even though the name of the tenth was removed from the tenth animal when it was called the eleventh:
messages.quote: As long as the name of the tenth has not been removed

messages.text: § The baraita teaches: If two animals emerged from the pen together as the tenth, and one did not come out before the other, and he called them both the tenth, the tenth and eleventh animals are intermingled with each other. There is apparently a dispute between tanna’im as to how these animals must be treated.
messages.quote: If two animals emerged from the pen together as the tenth

notes.he: היינו כגון אמר מר ואשמעתא דרבא קמהדר דקאמר לעיל יצאו שנים בעשירי קראן עשירי עשירי ואחד עשר מעורבין זה בזה והשתא קא פריש תנא חדא דהנהו שנים שמעורבין ירעו עד שיסתאבו ותניא אידך כו':
notes.en: Two emerged at the tenth: this goes back, as the Master said, to Rava’s teaching above, who said: two emerged at the tenth and he called them tenth, the tenth and eleventh are intermingled with each other. And now the tanna explains: one [baraita] teaches that those two intermingled animals graze until they become blemished, and another teaches, etc.

notes.he: יצאו שנים בעשירי וקראו י':
notes.en: Two emerged at the tenth and he called them tenth.

messages.text: One tanna taught that both animals must be left to graze until they develop a blemish, and then they may be eaten by the owner. And one tanna taught that both animals must be sacrificed. And it is taught in another baraita that both animals must die.

It is not difficult: This ruling, of the tanna who taught that both animals must be left to graze until they develop a blemish, is in accordance with the opinion of the Rabbis, who say: One may not bring sacrificial animals to a situation where the time in which they may be eaten is decreased, thereby increasing the likelihood of disqualification.

notes.he: שאילו היו קריבים צריך לאוכלן כחומר שבהם דצריך להרים מהם חזה ושוק וליתן לכהנים ומתוך שהכהנים מועטין הן אין נאכל אלא לכהנים שמא לא יהו מצויין אוכלין לאותן חזה ושוק ויפסלו בלינה לאחר שני ימים ולילה אחד והשתא מביא אחד מהם שהוא מעשר לבית הפסול דהא מעשר ודאי אינו צריך הרמת חזה ושוק לכהנים אלא הכל נאכל לכל אדם ומצויין לו אוכלין הרבה ולא ליתי לעולם לידי פסול לינה. במס' זבחים פ' כל הזבחים שנתערבו (זבחים דף עה:) גמרי' פלוגתא דר"ש ורבנן דתנן אשם שנתערב בשלמים ר"ש אומר שניהם ישחטו בצפון ויאכל כחמור שבהן אמרו לו אין מביאים קדשים לבית הפסול:
notes.en: One may not bring sacrificial animals to disqualification: for if they were sacrificed, they would have to be eaten according to the stricter of the two, which requires that the breast and thigh be lifted from them and given to the priests; and since priests are few, and [that portion] is eaten only by priests, perhaps there will not be enough eaters for that breast and thigh, and they will be disqualified by being left over after two days and one night. And so he brings one of them, the tithe, to disqualification, for a tithe certainly does not require lifting the breast and thigh for the priests; rather, all of it is eaten by anyone, and many eaters are available for it, and it would never come to be disqualified by being left over. In tractate Zevaḥim, in the chapter Kol HaZevaḥim SheNitarevu (Zevaḥim 75b), we learn the dispute of Rabbi Shimon and the Rabbis, as we learned: A guilt offering that became intermingled with a peace offering: Rabbi Shimon says both are slaughtered in the north and eaten according to the stricter of the two. They said to him: One may not bring sacrificial animals to disqualification.

notes.he: כרבנן דאמרי אין מביאין קדשים לבית הפסול דעשירי ואחד עשר מעורבין מעשר ושלמים ואי אמרינן דתרוייהו קריבין ובעי למיהב מתרוייהו חזה ושוק משום ספק שלמים זימנין דהוי לכהנים רוב קרבנות ולא מספקי למיכלינה להני חזה ושוק בתוך זמנן ואתי לידי פסול לשרפה ומעשר ראוי לאוכלו לישראל כולן חוץ מאימורין וישראל מרובין הן ויכלי למיכליה בתוך זמנו והשתא ממעטינן באכילתו ויהבינן להו לכהנים ואתי לידי פסול להכי ירעו עד דיסתאבו ופריק חד מנייהו וליהוו תרווייהו נאכלין במומן לבעלים והא פלוגתא דרבנן ור"ש הוא במס' זבחים בפ' כל הזבחים שנתערבו בחטאות אשם שנתערב בשלמים ר"ש אמר שניהם ישחטו בצפון ויאכלו כחמור שבהן אע"ג דאתי שלמים לידי פסול דלא מסתפקי למיכלינהו לזמנו של אשם אמרו לו אין מביאין קדשים לבית הפסול:
notes.en: In accordance with the Rabbis, who say one may not bring sacrificial animals to disqualification: for the intermingled tenth and eleventh are a tithe and a peace offering; and if we say both are sacrificed, one must give breast and thigh from both because one may be the peace offering. Sometimes the priests have most of the offerings and cannot manage to eat this breast and thigh within their time, and it comes to disqualification [and] burning; whereas the tithe is fit to be eaten entirely by Israelites, except the sacrificial portions, and Israelites are many and can eat it within its time. Now we reduce its eating and give [part of it] to the priests, and it comes to disqualification. Therefore they graze until they become blemished, he redeems one of them, and both are eaten by the owners in their blemished state. And this is the dispute of the Rabbis and Rabbi Shimon in tractate Zevaḥim, in the chapter Kol HaZevaḥim SheNitarevu BeḤatta’ot: a guilt offering that became intermingled with a peace offering, Rabbi Shimon says both are slaughtered in the north and eaten according to the stricter of the two, even though the peace offering comes to disqualification, as they cannot manage to eat it within the time of the guilt offering. They said to him: One may not bring sacrificial animals to disqualification.

messages.text: If both animals were to be sacrificed they would have to be eaten in accordance with the stringencies of both the animal tithe offering and the peace offering. They would have to be eaten within two days, like a peace offering, while the breast and the thigh would be given to the priests, as in the case of an animal tithe offering. Since only priests may eat those portions it is possible that they would be unable to eat them within the permitted time, and the remaining meat would become disqualified.
Continues on 61a: the tanna who rules that both animals are sacrificed follows Rabbi Shimon, who holds that one may bring sacrificial animals to a situation where disqualification is more likely.
